before:
dialect grammar
grammar stdio.tiff.snapshot
extension tiff
start document

# TIFF has no textual syntax of its own — `store::ArtifactDsl::print_dsl`/`parse_dsl`
# (../../🦀️.rs, the `HandcraftedArtifactCodecs` region) hex-encode/decode the REAL
# binary TIFF 6.0 file bytes (byte-order mark + IFD chain, TIFF6 §2) verbatim, byte-for-byte —
# this is png's own honest precedent from Phase 1's survey (P2-W0 §1b: "hex-dump grammar per
# png's own precedent"), not an aspiration. See ../💾️binary/📡️.protocol.semio for that
# same binary's real structural grammar (runtime-endian header + first-IFD entry table).
comment none

# `dsl::fixture_sweep`'s `dsl_body_from_fixture` feeds the Recognizer
# "<envelope-id>\n<body>" (`SemioEnvelope::envelope_id` = "stdio.tiff", the real preamble
# line's own trailing "v<n>" already stripped by the harness) — the shared lexer treats the
# preamble's newline as trivia, so `envelope-mark` and the hex body sit directly adjacent in
# the significant token stream, matching json/csv/png's own grammars' identical convention.
envelope-mark = "stdio.tiff"
document = envelope-mark hex-body

# The rest of the DSL text is one lowercase-hex digit run — the real TIFF file's bytes (8-byte
# header + IFD chain + generic tag/type/value entries + strip pixel data), hex-encoded
# losslessly (`encode_tiff`/`decode_tiff`, ⚙️engine/🦀️.rs). `hex` (bare `hex`,
# deliberately NOT defined as a production here) is the framework's built-in `hex` MACRO
# (`📖️grammar/🦀️.rs`'s `default_macros`/`macro_hex_ok`) — the dialect-recipe's own
# documented rule (`📖️grammar-recipe.md` §1.3(f)/§3 pitfall 2): a hand-rolled
# `{INT | IDENT}*`-shaped production would silently mis-lex a `<digits>e<digits>` byte run as
# one FLOAT token instead of alternating INT/IDENT; the macro's own largest-span-first
# backtracking (`Recognizer::match_macro_span`) handles it correctly with no grammar-file
# workaround needed — same mechanism json's/csv's/png's own `hex` doc comments already document
# for their op/diff payloads.
hex-body = hex

before:
dialect protocol
protocol stdio.tiff.snapshot
version 1
schema stdio.tiff
start header

# Real TIFF 6.0 byte layout — field-for-field against the REAL codec (../../../⚙️engine/
# 🦀️.rs's `decode_tiff`/`encode_tiff`), using M2's `endian {...}` construct exactly
# as the P2-W0 recon's dedicated TIFF paragraph and the P2-M2 report's own worked TIFF test
# describe. Models the bytes as if the walk already starts AT the payload (past the SEMIO
# envelope — see `🧬️semio/📡️protocol/📡️.protocol.semio`, described once,
# framework-level; per M3's own guidance, this file does NOT re-describe it).
#
# ── Header (TIFF6 §2, 8 bytes) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# `byte_order` is the real `II`/`MM` marker (`decode_tiff`/`encode_tiff`, ⚙️engine/
# 🦀️.rs:344-348) — M2 item 6's `endian {...}` construct, THE dialect capability
# TIFF's own recon paragraph names this needing: it genuinely reads the 2-byte marker AND
# mutates the walker's runtime endian mode for every subsequent plain (non-`Be`-suffixed)
# `Prim` read for the REST of this walk (`magic`/`first_ifd_offset` below, plus every field
# inside `entry_count`), not merely a per-field static choice the way PNG/JPEG's BE-everywhere
# format needed (`p2-w0-recon-report.md`'s dedicated "TIFF byte-order marker" paragraph).
framing record
header fixed 8
field byte_order endian { "II"=le "MM"=be }
field magic u16
field first_ifd_offset u32

# ── First IFD's entry count (TIFF6 §2) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# One real, individually protocol-walked field: the 2-byte entry count leading IFD 0. Past
# this point the file is genuinely NOT a linear forward-describable structure at the
# declarative protocol-dialect level — three independent, already-catalogued mechanism gaps
# compound here (P2-W0 §1b's own TIFF row, "specific gap(s)" column):
#   (a) `entry_count` real 12-byte IFD entries (tag/type/count/value-or-offset) are a
#       HOMOGENEOUS but per-entry-count-varying-shape record repeated `entry_count` times —
#       `Prim::Array` only repeats one FIXED-WIDTH SCALAR, never a multi-field RECORD
#       (`protocol-array-of-records`, hit independently by zip/csv's own nested-record-array
#       gap — this is TIFF's own instance of the identical root cause);
#   (b) each entry's `value-or-offset` 4-byte field is DUAL-MEANING depending on whether
#       `element_size(type) * count <= 4` (TIFF6 §2's own documented inline-vs-offset rule,
#       `read_tag_values`, ⚙️engine/🦀️.rs:140-154) — genuine out-of-line
#       offset-pointer resolution, the SAME class of gap ZIP's `cd_offset`/`local_off` need,
#       scoped down here to per-entry tag VALUES rather than a whole section;
#   (c) the IFD chain itself is pointer-chased (`next_ifd_offset`, repeat until 0) rather than
#       a single forward pass or a tag-dispatched/sentinel-terminated `repeat` — no "repeat via
#       next-pointer until sentinel 0" construct exists;
#   (d) pixel strip data is reached via `StripOffsets`/`StripByteCounts` tag VALUES (more
#       offset pointers, decode_pixels_from_ifd, ⚙️engine/🦀️.rs:264-338), several
#       further offset-resolution hops past even (b).
# Per the recipe's own documented workaround for this exact shape (§5 `protocol-array-of-
# records`/`protocol-prim-ref-recursion` rows): model the real fixed leading field, then treat
# the rest (every IFD entry, the next-IFD-offset chain, every out-of-line tag value, and the
# pixel strip data) as ONE opaque trailing `chain` — the Rust `decode_tiff`/`encode_tiff` side
# stays genuinely, fully structured (generic tag/type/value decode for all 12 field types, IFD
# chain walk, inline-vs-offset resolution, strip reassembly) and round-trip tested
# independently; this protocol description's honest reach stops at the real, bounded header.
#
# A second `header fixed N` block (not a NAMED `record` block) is used here deliberately:
# `walk_protocol`'s own `Framing::Record` handling special-cases a NAMED `Block::Record` by
# jumping `pos` straight to `bytes.len()` on first sight (treating the whole remaining buffer as
# that one record's body, "record IS the rest" — the shape json's own `framing record / chain
# payload utf8` text-native exemplar relies on) rather than genuinely walking its declared
# fields — real, individually field-checked fields under `Framing::Record` belong in an
# (optionally repeated) `header fixed N` block instead, exactly as `📖️grammar-recipe.md` §2.5's
# own `format u8 | tag u8 | chain payload bytes` op-frame exemplar does.
header fixed 2
field entry_count u16

chain rest bytes
